name: Ilizarov external fixator lengthening

lead: Ilizarov lengthening adds real, permanent height by lengthening the leg bones. It is well established in orthopaedics for lengthening and deformity correction, and in looksmaxxing circles it is discussed as the older alternative to internal lengthening nails.

The apparatus is a modular external frame of rings, wires and rods attached to the bone. After the bone is cut, the frame separates the pieces about 1 mm per day and new bone forms in the gap, a process called distraction osteogenesis. Gavriil Ilizarov developed it for non-union and deformity, and it was introduced to US medicine in 1987.

paras: The frame is adjusted several times a day during lengthening, then stays on through consolidation while the new bone hardens, and is removed in a second operation. Months in a frame is the core feature that later techniques aimed to reduce.

A landmark 1990 paper classified difficulties as problems, obstacles and complications, with high rates in the foundational series. Reference sources list inflammation at pin sites, muscle transfixion and joint contracture. Cosmetic stature use is discussed separately from trauma and deformity use.

angle.text: A ring fixator gradually separates cut bone so new bone fills the gap, adding permanent leg length and height. The method is well established in orthopaedics, with a long frame-wearing period and documented complication rates.

lead: The Ilizarov apparatus is a circular external fixator, built from stainless steel or titanium rings attached to bone by wires and pins and linked by threaded rods [1]. Developed by Gavriil Ilizarov in Kurgan, it is used for lengthening, deformity correction, non-union, bone transport and complex fractures [1]. The Taylor Spatial Frame is a later development [1].

In limb lengthening, the bone is cut and the frame is adjusted at roughly 1 mm per day; new bone forms in the gap under tension, a process Ilizarov described experimentally in canine studies as the 'tension-stress effect' [2][1]. In cosmetic height-lengthening discussion, the method is mainly contrasted with lengthening over nail and internal nails, which aim to reduce time in a frame.

paras: Ilizarov is reported to have discovered distraction osteogenesis when a patient's frame was lengthened instead of shortened and new bone appeared. His treatment of the high jumper Valeriy Brumel in 1968 (3.5 cm lengthening) and of the explorer Carlo Mauri in 1980 drew attention, and the technique reached US medicine in 1987 [1]. His laboratory work on stability of fixation and soft-tissue preservation was published in 1989 [2].

Wires are tensioned between rings; the frame is adjusted by the patient or carer a few times daily; after lengthening the device stays on during consolidation and is removed surgically [1]. Uses include nonunions with bone loss [3], bone transport for tibial defects [4] and severe open fractures [5][6].

A widely cited paper subclassified difficulties during Ilizarov lengthening into problems (resolved without surgery), obstacles (requiring operative intervention) and true complications [7]. Reference sources list inflammation, muscle transfixion and joint contracture [1]. Comparative studies of lengthening over nail versus conventional Ilizarov lengthening were done to reduce frame time.

Evidence mainly concerns trauma and deformity rather than cosmetic height. Studies include Ilizarov treatment of tibial nonunions with bone loss [3], bone transport for tibial defects [4], and the problems, obstacles and complications series [7]. Registered trials examine Ilizarov fixation in open paediatric tibial fractures [8], hybrid Ilizarov versus plating in tibial plateau fractures [9], bifocal versus trifocal bone transport [10], and an Ilizarov frame versus uniplanar fixator comparison [11].

timeline.event: Ilizarov treats Valeriy Brumel, lengthening his leg by 3.5 cm [1].
Apparatus and techniques introduced to US medicine [1].
Problems, obstacles and complications classification published [7].
